messages:
nina: running a restore validation for snapshot-2026-03-19-tenant12 — midway we got a decrypt deny on a subset of objects
omar: error pasted from logs: `AccessDeniedException: User: arn:aws:sts::123:assumed-role/restore-runner is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on key arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123:key/kk77`
felix: did we recently tighten the restore-runner IAM? i remember an RBAC cleanup that removed direct kms:* actions and moved to ephemeral grants
tara: PR 754 changed role permissions to disallow kms:Decrypt and force ephemeral flow. link: https://git.redd/infra/pulls/754
nina: ephemeral-grant-service logs show `CreateGrant` succeeded but the restore workers reported `InvalidGrantTokenException` on the later objects
felix: that usually means either TTL too short or grant propagation problem. what was the grant TTL?
infra-oncall: grant-service response: grantId=gr-2026-03-19-88 ttlSeconds=600; restore started immediately but the snapshot was pulled with backpressure from S3 and final workers ran ~13m later
omar: so grant expired. our restore pipeline parallelizes downloads and can exceed 10m for big snapshots. we assumed grants short-lived was fine — wrong assumption
tara: mitigation: 1) manual CreateGrant with ttlSeconds=3600 for the affected key 2) resume restore 3) mark this drill as P1 for policy review
ina: manual grant worked, full restore completed, checksums matched :white_check_mark:
felix: follow-ups: - increase default TTL for restore-role grants to 1800s while we implement refresh logic - add grant-expiry metadata in restore-runner logs (grant_expiry_ts) - gating in rotation: require a sample decrypt before finalizing CMK rotation
marc: (sec-bot) recommend also adding audit tagging: attach job_id and snapshot_id to CreateGrant request fields so CloudTrail correlation is trivial
sec-bot: Drill logged (id=drill-2026-03-21-restore-03). Reminder: attach CloudTrail CreateGrant events and S3 manifests to the ticket.
omar: also a policy note: when changing RBAC to remove direct kms:* access, we must update runbooks and add integration tests that exercise long-running restores under the ephemeral flow
tara: i'll open two tickets: one for ttl/defaults and one for restore-runner refresh path. i'll also add a CI check that PRs touching key policies or role perms trigger a restore smoke test in staging.
felix: audit query I ran to find impacted keys: `fields @timestamp, eventName, userIdentity.arn, requestParameters.grantId | filter eventName = "CreateGrant" and requestParameters.keyId like "%kk77%"`
nina: leaving thread open 48h. will post ticket ids and timeline once I finish log collection and validate there are no other expired-grant restores in the past 72h.
